entities.name: Brochfael ab Elisedd
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Brochfael ab Elisedd, a king of Powys in the mid-8th century, played a pivotal role in the region's governance and legacy. 


Born around 740 CE, Brochfael inherited the throne from his father, Elisedd ap Gwylog, and ruled until his death in 773 CE. During his reign, he implemented various policies aimed at strengthening Powys' economy and military. 


One of his most notable achievements was the construction of the Brochfael's Bridge, which connected Powys to neighboring kingdoms. 


Upon his death, his son, Cadell ap Brochfael, succeeded him as king. Brochfael's name was also inscribed in the Pillar of Eliseg, a testament to his legacy. 


In the annals of Powys' history, Brochfael ab Elisedd stands as a significant figure, marking the beginning of a new era for the kingdom. 


In the realm of cultural heritage, his name continues to be celebrated through the Pillar of Eliseg, a tangible reminder of his enduring impact.


The Pillar of Eliseg, erected by Brochfael's father, Elisedd ap Gwylog, bears a striking inscription that includes Brochfael's name.
